summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Hanna Dewo/143)

data.turoyo: I+dukṯo dm̩bā́ḏwayno hawxa kulle ma… məhnənwa mačəlṣiwa.
data.translation: every place I repaired like so, it was entirely... it could whatsit... it would shine.

rationale: First Infectum-wa box; tinned surfaces shine, preserving the source hesitation.

data.translation: Diese aber funkelten zwischen dem Heu.

rationale: Fill Infectum; overt eyes as subject and a short independent Turoyo clause.

data.turoyo: Ḥiraḥir das səsye, aš šəlfat dar rumḥe komačalṣi, xd ak kukwe di šmayo, məqqaṣ komačalṣi, haqqa aš šəlfe dar rumḥe komačalṣi.
data.translation: Das wiehern der Pferde..., die spitzender Lanzen glitzern wie die Sterne am Himmel; so wie die glitzern, glitzern die Lanzenspitzen.

rationale: Fill Infectum with metallic lance tips and an explicit comparison to stars; one example covers three tokens.

data.turoyo: Kul ḥabṯo mənne, u isan laybe ḥoyər aʕla, həngi komabarqo, mačalṣo.
data.translation: Jeder Kern..., man kann gar nicht darauf Blicken, so sehr blitzt und funkelt er.

rationale: Fifth Infectum example; shining kernels/pearls extend the same literal subject range.

summary: III is used with the shining entity as subject and no caused participant despite its stem shape.
Infectum-wa mačəlṣiwa describes shining as a recurrent result of tinning. The ordinary Infectum can combine with fayəš to present onset, as in the already quoted 75/148.
Two cooccurring verbs, mačləṣ and mabrəq, reinforce the same visual effect; no light-verb collocation is established.
The cauldron passage repairs the subject and uses a plural-shaped form after i dukṯo; confirm agreement and the precise surface referred to.
PrS 67/48 translates the eyes with an anaphoric Diese. The Turoyo supplies the noun, but its possessor is not established by this verse alone.
Water, golden skin, eyes, stars, lance tips, precious kernels and repaired metal surfaces all instantiate literal shine; no new sense.
